author: claude-design / c130_reference_audit
scope: Public visual/documentary references for non-operational C-130 family game-asset modular loadouts
selected_eras: AC-130J selected-era fit must remain distinct

sources.title: C-130 Hercules
supports: Common family airframe; J engine/propeller/cockpit changes require coherent variant modules.
limits: Published fact-sheet dimension conversions contain apparent typographical errors; do not use metric conversions as a precision geometry ruler.

sources.title: JTF-Quartz weapon system: AC-130W Stinger II
supports: AC-130W is a highly modified C-130H with dual EO/IR sensors, 30mm and 105mm systems.
limits: Documents the 2020-era W configuration; does not make gunship conversion a field-swappable panel job.

sources.title: AC-130J Ghostrider
supports: J-based gunship family and mission package identity.
limits: W and J exterior geometry must not be silently conflated. Exact selected-era fit needs photographic comparison.

sources.title: C/KC-130 Hercules / Super Hercules
supports: Tanker/transport roles and modular Harvest HAWK mission-kit precedent.
limits: Use dated sources for historical Harvest HAWK fit; no claim of current 2026 fleet status.

sources.title: Harvest HAWK mission-kit installation report
supports: Derringer package replaces a paratroop door. Early sensor located in left underwing fuel tank. Left refueling pylon is replaced by a weapon launcher.
limits: This is a specific historical configuration, not a universal station plan for every C-130.

sources.title: MC-130J Commando II
sources.publisher: 193rd Special Operations Wing / Air National Guard
supports: One aircraft includes UARRSI receiver installation, tanker pods and EO/IR. Six-blade propellers and J flight deck.
limits: Receptacle and tanker pods can coexist; exact hatch motion is not specified.

sources.title: MC-130E Combat Talon I
supports: Receiver receptacle and helicopter refueling role; substantial structural and mission-suite modifications.
limits: Legacy E historical configuration; not evidence that all module combinations exist on one operational aircraft.

sources.title: The Praetorian STARShip: The Untold Story of the Combat Talon
sources.author: Jerry L. Thigpen
sources.publisher: Air University Press / U.S. Air Force
supports: Combat Talon nose yoke is permanent and retractable; folds back along fuselage. Drooped radome distinguishes the historical Fulton nose. Fending lines connect outer wingtips to near the nose sky-anchor assembly. Cabin recovery kit is removable.
limits: Figures 2-3 depict earlier C-130A/B installation, not an exact MC-130E orthographic template. No exact E yoke hinge angle or full endpoint photo pair accepted.

sources.title: May 3, 1966: Fulton recovery system milestone
limits: Does not establish a modern J installation.

sources.title: 109th Airlift Wing aircrew tests new engine
supports: Historical LC-130 JATO and later engine/NP2000 upgrades. NP2000 introduced to this fleet in 2019; JATO production ended in 1991.
limits: A 2003 JATO image is not a current-fleet baseline. No real takeoff-performance model or operational JATO procedure is supplied.

sources.title: Empowered Airmen from 109th AW modernize LC-130 for future fight
limits: Eight-blade NP2000 LC-130H is an H-family exception; blade count alone is not an H/J identity rule.

sources.title: 4th AMU Night MX
supports: Official caption confirms an aerial refueling door on AC-130U.
limits: Image host was unavailable; caption is not evidence of hinge/sliding direction. Not used for geometry acceptance.

claims.decision: Closed ramp must mate with the upswept aft belly silhouette. Retain sensible skin seams and hinge/seal details; reject a broad daylight gap or detached slab. Exact tolerances remain unverified.

One master family model can expose loadouts for skin infills/apertures, systems and associated interior pieces. Operational variants remain coherent era-tagged presets; arbitrary combinations are custom game configurations.

Replace complete panel systems: closed skin infill versus opening/frame/seal, installed gun and relevant visible cabin geometry. Do not leave weapons or duplicate blank skin occupying an active aperture.
Receiver interface and tanker pods are independent capabilities; MC aircraft may carry both. Do not apply a global receiver-versus-tanker exclusion.
Use independent port/starboard station occupancy. Historical Harvest HAWK weapon station replaces left refueling pylon; early left-tank sensor is another specific dependent module.
Pod, unreeled hose, collapsed basket and deployed basket are separate geometry/state concerns. Low/high-speed basket choice is documented; exact pair of shapes remains unaccepted.

Historical legacy configuration needs drooped nose/yokes, nose-to-wing fending lines and recovery cabin/ramp equipment. Yokes spread left/right ahead of nose and fold back along fuselage. Exact pivot/travel is illustrative until endpoint references are secured.
Author bracket/bottle banks and loaded/spent/reset visuals as a historical kit. Flame/smoke timing is game-authored; no operational/performance fidelity claim.

unresolved.remaining: Acquire unobscured open/closed endpoints or an authoritative motion depiction; do not call the authored travel a verified sliding or hinged mechanism.
Exact MC-130E extended and folded-back photographs and hinge geometry; inspected USAF history establishes foldback concept only.
Clear calibrated photographs of each selected hardware type; swap photo only proves choice/interchange.
Compare implemented model against inspected references at matched angles. This ledger is not final photographic acceptance.

rejected_as_endpoint_evidence.reason: Actual photo shows balloon display in hangar, not installed nose yoke.
Caption says secures ramp but actual frame depicts open airdrop; not closed-ramp proof.

access_limits: Several archive/media hosts returned HTTP errors; no exact Fulton endpoint image was accepted from inaccessible thumbnails or generated search-image descriptions.
DVIDS public preview files were downloaded and inspected; no sign-in download endpoints were used.
